power.pluralism.5.why: Whether an organised, legitimate opposition is a needed check on rulers. distribution.tax.7.why: Whether a ceiling on farmland per person or family is justified. Agrarian-reform camps (Leninist, Maoist, Sun Yat-sen, Nasser, Chavez, Proudhonian use-and-occupancy, Harrington's agrarian law) say yes; landed conservatives, aristocrats and all property-first liberals and libertarians say no; nationalists and technocrats mostly have no stake.

notes.CLR: Harrington's Oceana (1656) enshrines an 'agrarian law' capping landed income, after the Licinian-Sextian law: 3.
notes.TP: Sun Yat-sen's 'equalisation of land rights' and 'land to the tiller' are the core of the livelihood principle: 3.
notes.NA: Nasser's 1952 Agrarian Reform Law capped holdings at 200 feddans (later 100 then 50): 3.
notes.TI: Yugoslavia's 1953 law limited private holdings to 10 hectares: 3.
notes.MU: Proudhon's occupancy-and-use rule allows only as much land as one can work: 3.
notes.MA: Mao's 1950 Agrarian Reform Law redistributed landlord land to peasants: 3.
notes.BC: Burke defended entails, primogeniture and great landed estates as stabilising ballast: -3.
notes.BIC: Bismarck's Junker landowners and the east-Elbian estates were the Prussian state conservative base: -3.
notes.LF: Rothbard: land titled by homesteading and exchange can be held in any quantity: -3.
notes.GE: Georgists tax land rent rather than cap land area, so they refuse a ceiling: -1.
notes.MC: Mencius 1A3 and 3A3: the well-field (jingtian) system equalises holdings and fixes each household a hundred mu: 3.
notes.PE: Diem's Ordinance 57 (1957) set a 100-hectare ceiling on holdings: 2.
notes.EC: The Tang equal-field system and Dong Zhongshu's proposed cap on holdings are the examination state's agrarian ideal: 2.

distribution.labour.3.why: Whether the state should fix a minimum wage. Social democrats, New Dealers, Peronists, Catholic social teaching and most corporatist camps back it (3/2); libertarians, classical liberals and Burkeans see it as interference in wage contracts; anarchists and council communists would abolish the wage system itself; and the Nordic model is split because unions there prefer collective bargaining.

notes.NDL: The 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act created the federal minimum wage and 44-hour week: 3.
notes.PER: Peron's 1944-46 'salario minimo vital y movil' became a constitutional social right in the 1949 charter: 3.
notes.CST: Rerum Novarum (1891) and Quadragesimo Anno demand a 'just wage' enough to support a family, enforced where bargaining fails: 3.
notes.NM: Sweden, Denmark and Norway have no statutory minimum wage; unions defend collective bargaining over legal floors: -1, split.
notes.BC: Burke's Scarcity (1795) rejects fixing wages by law as against the natural order of labour and trade: -3.
notes.TH: The Thatcher government abolished the Wages Councils in 1986-93, rejecting statutory floors: -2.
notes.SDD: Swiss voters rejected a national minimum wage by 76% in 2014, though Neuchatel and Jura have one: -1, split.
notes.AUC: Singapore has no minimum wage, using its Progressive Wage Model: -1.
notes.NAZ: The 1933 Labour Trustees (Treuhander der Arbeit) fixed binding wage scales in place of bargaining: 2.
notes.SMCD: Germany's Mindestlohn (2015) was introduced by a CDU/CSU-SPD coalition: 2.
notes.KS: Arthashastra Book 2 has the Superintendent fix wages by work and the king bind employers: 2.

power.pluralism.8.why: Whether a one-party state with internal debate and elections can count as democratic. Marxist-Leninist, Vietnamese, Cuban, Yugoslav and Tanzanian camps say yes (their own doctrine of inner-party democracy), liberal, social-democratic, republican and anarchist camps say a democracy needs more than one party (-3), and Luxemburg-style and Trotskyist camps use inner-party democracy as the very thing the single-party state lacks.

notes.NLS: Ho Chi Minh and the Communist Party of Vietnam treat 'dan chu trong Dang' and democratic centralism as a real democracy under party leadership: 3.
notes.RS: Deng's Four Cardinal Principles and Hu-era 'intra-party democracy' (dang nei minzhu) are the PRC's answer to multiparty democracy: 3.
notes.UJ: Nyerere's 'Democracy and the Party System' (1963) holds a single party with real internal contests is more democratic than rival parties: 3.
notes.TI: Kardelj's 'democracy without parties' placed self-management, delegates and the LCY in place of rival parties: 3.
notes.GU: Cuba's 1976 and 2019 constitutions name the PCC the leading force while Marti's 'one party for all' justifies it: 3.
notes.LU: Luxemburg, The Russian Revolution (1918): without free elections and unlimited freedom of the press, life dies out in every public institution: -3.
notes.TR: In The Revolution Betrayed (1936) Trotsky says the Soviet Union needs a plurality of Soviet parties and the end of bureaucratic rule: -2, split.
notes.PM: Daniel Bell's The China Model argues one-party selection plus internal competition is better than elections for top posts: 2.
notes.CM: A constitutional monarchy's parliament rests on competing parties as a matter of constitutional practice: -3.
notes.NAZ: The Fuhrerprinzip rejects party debate and elections, so Nazism denies that inner-party elections create democracy: -1.
notes.EC: The examination state's selection by competition is meritocracy, not democracy; some modern heirs call it democratic enough: 1.
